<description>
An ipc client can pass any timeout to `waitTipChanged`, but the code assumes it is never negative:

```
Assume(timeout >= 0ms); // No internal callers should use a negative timeout
```

On debug builds, a negative or NaN timeout fails this check and aborts the node. I reproduced this with a timeout of -1.0.

On release builds the check is skipped. Negative values are clamped to zero, but NaN is not, because every comparison with NaN is false. It ends up as the deadline passed to `wait_until`.

`waitNext` has no Assume, but it also doesn't check its timeout. A NaN timeout waits one extra fee tick (about one second) before returning.

`waitTipChanged` and `waitNext` now throw an error for negative or NaN timeouts. The internal `Assume` in `WaitTipChanged` still checks internal callers. The interface documents the errors, and the functional test covers rejection of negative and NaN timeouts and acceptance of positive infinity in both methods.

I'm not aware of any client that sends these values (sv2-tp, for example, requires an interval of at least one second), so this is hardening against bad input from ipc clients.

_This is similar to #36520, which handles invalid arguments to the Chain interface for the same reason._

Links

- https://ipcbugs.ofsky.org/bugs/bitcoin-2026-wait-timeout-assume/
</description>

[2026-11-25] rc:4699557226 inline on test/functional/interface_ipc_mining.py by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-25):
In commit "mining: reject negative and NaN wait timeouts from IPC clients" (2bfe24e3ad8be86c76a6530ea056964c50cc1ca9)

These "Infinite timeout is accepted" tests, here and in the [`waitTipChanged` test above](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/2bfe24e3ad8be86c76a6530ea056964c50cc1ca9/test/functional/interface_ipc_mining.py#L167-L171), check that an infinite timeout isn't rejected, but not that the call actually waits. They would also pass if an infinite timeout made `waitNext` or `waitTipChanged` return immediately, for example because it was clamped to zero. `template6.interruptWait()` is evaluated as an argument to `wait_and_do`, and pycapnp sends the request right then, so the interrupt reaches the node before the wait starts and the wait returns immediately. I measured both waits returning in under 4ms instead of after `wait_and_do`'s 0.1s sleep. The [Ralph review](https://review.fish.foo/report/36940-758ae2c916eb8d2127ab1949b9630cf4348b8945-2999-4.html#finding-finding%3A2) pointed out the `waitNext` case.

Passing the method without calling it (`template6.interruptWait` rather than `template6.interruptWait()`) lets `wait_and_do` call it after the sleep. To catch the problem, `wait_and_do` could take an optional `check_order` argument that asserts the wait finished after `do_fn` was called, used here for the two new tests. I checked that this passes with the current code and fails with `wait finished 0.097s before do_fn was called` if `waitNext` treats an infinite timeout as zero:

```diff
diff --git a/test/functional/interface_ipc_mining.py b/test/functional/interface_ipc_mining.py

-            await wait_and_do(wait_for_tip_inf(), mining.interrupt())
+            await wait_and_do(wait_for_tip_inf(), mining.interrupt, check_order=True)

             self.log.debug("interrupt() should abort waitTipChanged()")
             async def wait_for_tip():
@@ -355,7 +355,7 @@ class IPCMiningTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
                     inf_waitoptions.feeThreshold = MAX_MONEY
                     template8 = await mining_wait_next_template(template6, stack, ctx, inf_waitoptions)
                     assert template8 is None
-                await wait_and_do(wait_for_block_inf(), template6.interruptWait())
+                await wait_and_do(wait_for_block_inf(), template6.interruptWait, check_order=True)
                 waitoptions.timeout = self.default_ipc_timeout_ms

                 self.log.debug("interruptWait should abort the current wait")
diff --git a/test/functional/test_framework/ipc_util.py b/test/functional/test_framework/ipc_util.py
--- a/test/functional/test_framework/ipc_util.py
+++ b/test/functional/test_framework/ipc_util.py
@@ -10,6 +10,7 @@ from dataclasses import dataclass
 from io import BytesIO
 from pathlib import Path
 import shutil
+import time
 from typing import Optional

 from test_framework.messages import CBlock
@@ -45,20 +46,31 @@ async def destroying(obj, ctx):
         await obj.destroy(ctx)

-async def wait_and_do(wait_fn, do_fn, sleep_time=0.1):
+async def wait_and_do(wait_fn, do_fn, sleep_time=0.1, check_order=False):
     """Call wait_fn, then sleep, then call do_fn in a parallel task. Wait for
-    both tasks to complete."""
+    both tasks to complete.
+
+    With check_order, assert that wait_fn finishes after do_fn is called, to
+    catch waits that return early instead of being ended by do_fn. Pass do_fn
+    as a callable for this: pycapnp sends an IPC request when the method is
+    called, so cap.method() passed directly reaches the server before the
+    wait starts."""
     wait_started = asyncio.Event()
     result = None
+    wait_done = None
+    do_called = None

     async def wait():
-        nonlocal result
+        nonlocal result, wait_done
         wait_started.set()
         result = await wait_fn
+        wait_done = time.monotonic()

     async def do():
+        nonlocal do_called
         await wait_started.wait()
         await asyncio.sleep(sleep_time)
+        do_called = time.monotonic()
         # Let do_fn be either a callable or an awaitable object
         if inspect.isawaitable(do_fn):
             await do_fn
@@ -66,6 +78,8 @@ async def wait_and_do(wait_fn, do_fn, sleep_time=0.1):
             do_fn()

     await asyncio.gather(wait(), do())
+    if check_order:
+        assert wait_done >= do_called, f"wait finished {do_called - wait_done:.3f}s before do_fn was called"

```

---

The interrupt tests already on master have the same problem: the [`interrupt()` test for `waitTipChanged`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/5ba05739881855cba25c3c05d6f82a61b8a0665f/test/functional/interface_ipc_mining.py#L168), the [`createNewBlock` cooldown test](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/5ba05739881855cba25c3c05d6f82a61b8a0665f/test/functional/interface_ipc_mining.py#L252-L258) and the [`interruptWait()` test](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/5ba05739881855cba25c3c05d6f82a61b8a0665f/test/functional/interface_ipc_mining.py#L349) all pass the IPC call itself, so the interrupt is sent before the wait starts. The cooldown test also has no cooldown to interrupt: the [previous step](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/5ba05739881855cba25c3c05d6f82a61b8a0665f/test/functional/interface_ipc_mining.py#L233-L245) submits the announced block, so the tip has caught up. With the interrupt sent at the right time, `createNewBlock` returns a template and the test fails; announcing a header for a new block first fixes it.

A follow-up could fix these three tests, make `check_order` the default so every `wait_and_do` caller gets the check, and require `do_fn` to be a callable (awaiting what it returns) so an IPC call can't be passed directly again. I tried that version with all five call sites passing the method uncalled and the cooldown test fixed, and the test passes. That could be done here as well, or separately.
